en: Up to this point in the course, we always
used HTMX to send requests behind the scenes
and update parts of the screen with the
response data.
And you could, of course, still also use,
for example, regular anchor elements
and navigate to a different page without
using HTMX for that. That would all be
possible.
But sometimes you might wanna use HTMX and
build a single-page application, with it.
You might wanna give your website users that
single-page application-like look and feel
where to them it feels like the new page is
loaded almost instantly, the page never
flashes as it's replaced with the new page
that was fetched from the server.
And as it turns out, you can do that with
HTMX. You cannot just use it to fetch fetch
parts of a page and update parts of a page,
but instead you can use it to update and
render the entire page and use it for page
navigations, as you will learn in this
section.
And in this section, I'll show you 2 main
approaches. The manual approach, which can
be useful and which is important to know,
but even better than that, the automatic
approach, you could say, where you use one
simple, important attribute provided by HTMX
to
almost magically turn your website into an
HTMX-managed single-page application. So
let's take a look at that now.
